## Failure Signatures

> Use this to identify root causes from observed failure patterns.

| Observed Symptom | Likely Cause | Investigation |
|-----------------|-------------|---------------|
| Loss diverges (NaN) after N steps | LR too high, missing gradient clip | Reduce LR 10×, add `torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_` |
| Accuracy stuck at random baseline | Wrong loss function or label mismatch | Print predictions and targets for one batch |
| Val loss lower than train loss | Data leakage into val set | Check data splitting logic |
| Metrics differ from paper by constant offset | Wrong metric formula (micro vs macro) | Compute metric on hand-crafted example with known answer |
| Training unstable, oscillating loss | Batch normalization statistics wrong | Switch `model.train()` / `model.eval()` placement |
| *[Add paper-specific patterns]* | | |

## Debugging Strategies

### Fast Iteration Protocol

1. Use `--dry-run` (10 steps) to verify execution path without full training
2. Test data pipeline with a single batch before any training
3. Verify metric implementation on synthetic data with known answer
4. Run baseline for 1 epoch before attempting proposed method

### Component-Level Validation

*[For each novel component in the paper, describe how to verify it in isolation.]*

- **[Component name]**: *[e.g., "Feed random input, check output shape and gradient flow"]*

## Claude Code Guidance

### Implementation Order

*[Specify which modules to implement first to avoid circular dependencies.]*

1. Config + seed utilities
2. Dataset (needed to verify data before model)
3. Baseline model (needed for M1 before M2)
4. Training loop (with baseline)
5. Evaluation (metric functions)
6. Proposed method components (after M1 passes)

*[Paper-specific anti-patterns that are tempting but wrong.]*
